item.title: Jean 0.4.6
item.description:
Jean 0.4.6

Changes since 0.4.5 (from d861961), merged into slack-tidy (6116176).

Slack bridge

- The bridge notices when its Slack connection dies and reconnects on its own (or restarts). `jean doctor` shows ✗ while it's down, and `jean watch` restarts a bridge that stays disconnected. (#59) - After a restart, `jean doctor` shows the bridge as starting instead of briefly ✗. If it keeps crashing at startup (a bad Slack token, say), doctor shows ✗ after 2 minutes instead of "starting" forever. (#62, #63) - `jean doctor` checks that Claude Code is 2.1.295 or later (needed for the guard to block when it can't run) and says to run `claude update` if not. (#61)

Security (the guard)

- A lane can start one exact Claude session, or have Jean restart one lane, once an owner approves that command (a new "session" approval). (#33, #53) - **Approvals asked for just before this update won't match after it** (command ids now keep spacing inside quotes): ask again. One time only. - Closes many ways a command could run something the guard didn't see: git remote helpers and settings that run programs, text piped or fed into a shell or an interpreter, `trap`, `watch`, `find -exec sh -c`, `$(…)` inside here-documents, AppleScript `do shell script`, awk `system()`, and variable tricks (array elements, `+=`, `printf -v`, export/declare). (#47, #50, #60) - Only an owner can turn overflow helpers on or change them, change the packages in Jean's own Python, or restart Jean's background services. Checking a service (`launchctl print`, `list`) is fine. (#54, #60) - A lane can write only its own handoff notes. The file-editing tools and shell commands follow the same rules, and a repository's own hooks need an owner's OK. (#41, #58) - More git holes closed: `git clone -c`/`--config` settings (any short form, bundled flags), `--git-dir`, `--separate-git-dir` by any short form, and a repo's `.git` put in place by mv/cp (any letter case, as macOS sees it). (#67)

Fixes

- The memory meter reads 1M-token context windows correctly. (#64) - No longer stopped by mistake: `claude --help` and other read-only claude subcommands (#65); a lane's own modules named like Jean's (`work.py`, `keys.py`, `connectors/`) (#66); `2>&1`, `git for-each-ref`, `git remote show`, `git rebase --exec 'make test'`, harmless sed edits, text in single quotes or in a quoted here-document (a PR body or release note naming a command), a PR title with an apostrophe, Jean's own Python run to look, a lane's own scripts and job temp folder. (#48, #50, #56, #60)

New

- Worker sessions (`jean spawn`): a lane with several independent tasks asks an owner once, naming the tasks; after the ✅ it starts one worker per task, each in its own git worktree and branch, closed when the approved hours are up. The ask lists each task's text, and workers get exactly that text and the reason you approved, even if the task changes later. A lane can ask for workers only for itself. Workers follow the lane's rules and still ask before merges and deploys. (#66, #68) - Settings › Connections: each tool has its own step-by-step setup page with live links (Setup steps button). (#55) - Overflow helpers: a busy lane can hand new tasks to a temporary second session (off until an owner turns it on). (#52, #57) - Updates: before an update rolls back, Jean checks the copy it would roll back to is complete and signed. (#49)

item.title: Jean 0.4.5
item.description:
Jean 0.4.5

Fixes

- Studio: in 0.4.4 every Studio message ended with no answer (Claude was started without the message). Fixed. A message typed before Studio has finished opening is now held and sent as soon as it is ready instead of being lost. The same bug stopped Settings › Keys from saving a key in 0.4.4; fixed too. (#30, #39) - Studio: a message typed early is never lost: if Studio can't open or no Claude is found, it goes back into the message box with a note. Pressing Stop just before a retry now always stops. (#40) - A specialist is never restarted to free up memory before it has written its handoff notes: Jean asks you to check on it instead. It is never started twice either. (#27) - Jean.app no longer crashes when a window closes while a command it started is being stopped. (#45) - `jean doctor` no longer tells a desktop Mac "Laptops don't have it" when it can't find the restart-after-power-failure setting. (#35)

Security

- The guard stops forged approvals and secret reads hidden behind wildcards, braces, variables, arrays, loops, `cd`, `xargs` and similar shell forms. (#38) - The guard stops writes into its own files through 17 tricky shell forms it used to miss. (#31) - The guard matches file names in any letter case, with accents, and through links, so CAPS or a shortcut can't sneak past it. (#37) - A read-only git command redirected into Jean's own files (for example, git log written over the approvals file) now counts as a write and is stopped. (#34) - False alarm fixed: commit messages and PR text that only mention Jean's own files are no longer blocked. Real writes to those files and secret reads are still stopped. (#32)

New

- Studio: a mic button types what you say into the message box (macOS asks for the microphone and speech recognition once), and Shift+Enter makes a new line while Enter still sends. (#36) - New setup guide page, "Your always-on Mac and restarts", and three new `jean doctor` checks: FileVault, automatic login, and restart after a power failure. (#29)

item.title: Jean 0.4.4
item.description:
Jean 0.4.4

  • Only you approve. A specialist can no longer act as you: code it writes for a tab stays a draft until you preview and publish it (hub › To approve), and an automation it changes turns off until you approve the new steps, which the Slack message now shows in full.
  • Jean.app proves itself to the hub without sending its key, and the hub's sign-in for your windows lives only in memory, so nothing on this Mac can copy it.
  • The Library never copies a file that points somewhere else, or anything from Jean's own folder.
  • Slack task cards say "Waiting on you" when a specialist needs your answer, and tick off every step when the task is done.
  • The phone hub setup accepts Cloudflare account tokens, and says plainly when a token is mistyped.

item.title: Jean 0.4.3
item.description:
Jean 0.4.3

  • **Updates install themselves.** From now on Jean checks every hour, installs updates and relaunches by itself.
  • **The hub on your phone (setup).** `jean tunnel setup` connects the hub to your own address behind Cloudflare sign-in, from one paste.
  • **Fewer false stops.** The guard no longer blocks read-only commands like awk, find and git branch --list, or notes that name a file. Real risks still need your check mark.
  • **Your plan, never an API key.** Lanes, relays and Studio never pick up an Anthropic API key from the Mac, so Jean always bills your Claude plan.
  • **Dev bench (off by default).** A nightly review of the lanes work, for Jeans developers.

item.title: Jean 0.4.2
item.description:
Jean 0.4.2

  • Slack works again: 0.4.1 stopped Jean from hearing messages, check marks and Approve/Deny buttons. Anything you sent in Slack since updating to 0.4.1, please send again.

item.title: Jean 0.4.1
item.description:
Jean 0.4.1

**Tidier Slack threads** - Send several messages in a row and Jean answers them together, once. - A "thanks" or "all good" gets a 👍 instead of a reply. - Each request ends as one message: the "On it" card turns into the answer. - Shorter answers, no repeated commands, and a new topic gets its own thread.

**Studio message queue** - Type while Studio is working: your message joins the task in progress. - If the task has just finished, it waits and runs next. Stop hands it back.
